scenes.line1: What happens if your consumer crashes?
scenes.say: If your Kafka consumer crashes, do you know exactly where it will resume reading messages?

scenes.label: Offset
scenes.sub: Tracks a consumer’s position in a partition.
scenes.say: Offsets track your consumer's position in each partition. They're how Kafka knows which messages you've already processed.
You can commit offsets automatically, or do it manually after processing. Auto-commit is easy, but manual commit gives you more control.
With auto-commit, you might lose messages if a failure happens. Manual commit, after processing, ensures you never miss a message—even if you see duplicates.

scenes.question: When should you commit offsets?
scenes.right: After processing messages, to guarantee at-least-once delivery.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: When should you commit offsets? The answer is after processing messages, not before. That way, you guarantee at-least-once delivery.
